nodes.label: entropylens
nodes.rationale: Entropy-based STATISTICAL interpretability for neural activations across PyTorch, TensorFlow and JAX — measures how concentrated or spread out activation distributions are without touching the model. Explicitly disclaims semantic interpretability by design: high entropy only means 'spread out over the batch'. Two metrics (batch-wise per neuron, per-example per row), both in nats AND normalized [0,1] (only the normalized scale is cross-layer comparable; nats never shown without their bound). Out of scope v1: mutual information, entropy-based regularization, RNN, conv/4D validation.

nodes.label: EntropyTracker (PyTorch hooks)
nodes.rationale: Non-invasive forward-hook tracker: attach/detach around an eval forward (or context manager); report().summary() / depth_trend() give normalized per-layer aggregates. Conv/4D+ feature maps skipped with explicit warning (spatial-independence not validated in v1). Drop-in wrappers EntropyReLU/EntropyTanh/EntropyGELU/EntropyActivation offer the same bitwise guarantees.

nodes.label: batch_wise_entropy
nodes.rationale: Per-neuron entropy over the batch: quantile-winsorized histogram + Miller-Madow, bound log(min(N,B)); returns entropy (nats), normalized [0,1], and reliable flag (False = 'not estimable', NOT 'low entropy').

nodes.label: per_example_entropy
nodes.rationale: Per-example entropy of the normalized activation vector across neurons, bound log(M); strategy ('relu' or 'abs') is MANDATORY because the two answers differ by up to 8.6x — a silent default would be a lie. NaN + valid mask where undefined (all-zero row).

nodes.label: confidence_interval
nodes.rationale: Per-neuron 95% CI via full-pipeline bootstrap (raw values resampled, quantile edges re-estimated per replicate, normal interval). Result of adversarial verification: closed-form Basharin under-covers badly (min 62.5%), percentile bootstrap collapses near the ceiling (min 4%). Read coverage as '>= 85%, conservative' (measured 90.5-100%), valid N>=200 (N~400 under extreme sparsity — detected from the histogram with a runtime warning).

nodes.label: Honest Limitations
nodes.rationale: Limitations are documented, tested and frozen rather than hidden: reliable flag is necessary-not-sufficient (can read True with 7-14% error on heavy-tailed/sparse data at N in [90,~200], all probed cases <5% from N>=256, regression test frozen); degenerate samples give zero-width CI (the flag, not the CI, is the signal); Cauchy data makes normalized entropy 4-5x more seed-variable (mitigation: value_range); winsorized binning caps the attainable max at 99.92% of log B on continuous uniform density.

nodes.label: Visualization Dashboard (entropylens.viz)
nodes.rationale: plot_layer_trend, plot_neuron_heatmap, top_neurons, dashboard — post-hoc rendering of tracked history (near-zero training overhead, matplotlib lazily imported). Honest pathology handling: rankings EXCLUDE unreliable neurons and report how many were excluded; heatmaps grey them out instead of pretending they are measurements.

nodes.label: Bitwise Invariance Guarantee (B1/B2/B3)
nodes.rationale: The tracked forward pass is bitwise identical to the untracked one and nothing ever enters the autograd graph. B1/B2: outputs with and without tracking bitwise identical; B3: gradients bitwise identical, entropy tensors never require grad (torch.no_grad on detached tensors). All covered by torch.equal tests — exact, not 'close'.

nodes.label: Numpy Core (core_np mirror)
nodes.rationale: core_np.py: numpy mirror of core.py validated equivalent to the torch core (D7). Enables TF/JAX backends with the same estimators (D1-D6), same LayerRecord schema (record.py, framework-neutral), same report and viz.

nodes.label: TFEntropyTracker (TensorFlow/Keras)
nodes.rationale: Experimental TF/Keras backend (entropylens.tf, pip install 'entropylens[tf]'): observe(x_probe) runs an extra inference-mode pass through a weight-sharing auxiliary model (D8) — the user model is NEVER modified, so training outputs and gradients are invariant by construction (exp7). Caveats: observation is inference-mode (BatchNorm/Dropout differ from the training pass); subclassed models and nested submodels unsupported in v1 (functional or Sequential only, top-level layers only).

nodes.label: JaxEntropyTracker (JAX/Flax)
nodes.rationale: Experimental JAX/Flax backend (entropylens.jax, pip install 'entropylens[jax]'): observe() consumes intermediates from capture() — same forward pass, no second forward. Captured Dense outputs are pre-activation, so per-example entropy requires an explicit strategy_map; unmapped paths are tracked batch-wise only with a one-time warning. Outputs and gradients bitwise-invariant with and without capture, including under jax.jit (exp8; empirical scoping in D9).

nodes.label: capture (Flax capture_intermediates helper)
nodes.rationale: capture(model, params, x) -> (y, intermediates): runs the SAME forward pass while collecting intermediates via Flax capture_intermediates; the intermediates are then fed to JaxEntropyTracker.observe().

nodes.label: strategy_map (explicit per-path strategies, JAX)
nodes.rationale: Because Flax captures are pre-activation (activations are functions, not modules), no activation->strategy table is possible: per-example entropy requires an explicit per-path strategy_map (e.g. {"Dense_0": "relu"}) and no silent default is ever applied (D3/D8). Unmapped paths degrade to batch-wise-only with a one-time warning.

nodes.label: Per-Backend Guarantees Table
nodes.rationale: Invariance per backend (D9): PyTorch B1/B2/B3 bitwise (hooks), unchanged; TensorFlow user model untouched by construction, frozen bitwise in exp7; JAX/Flax outputs/grads bitwise with and without capture, including under jit (exp8, empirical scoping in D9).
